assertions.name: counterexample_passes_parity_but_is_not_an_admissible_root
assertions.source: z = (3*q**2 + 1)/(2*q) satisfies z - bar(z) = h yet is neither q nor z_D, so bar-parity is necessary-not-sufficient

description: Structural discriminator for the Q_beta functional question (qou-99qc). With h = q - 1/q and bar: q -> 1/q, bar(h) = -h identically, so for N(z) = tr_M(Delta_S) = h^2/2 - h z one has bar(N) = -N iff z - bar(z) = h, equivalently iff z - h/2 is bar-INVARIANT. Measured exactly: BOTH admissible roots (z = q the augmentation, z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) the convention-D Markov point) satisfy it and give bar(Q_beta)/Q_beta = q^3; the PUBLISHED functional z = 1 and the excised convention C z_C = sqrt(q)/(q+1) both FAIL it, and fail the same way (both are bar-invariant, bar(z) = z). Also supplies closed forms for all three cells of the Delta_S column, which the corpus carried only as decimals: Q_beta/m_e = (q+1)/(2q^3) * M with M = |q^2-2q-1| (z=1, NOT palindromic), (q^2+1) (z=q), (q^4+1)/(q^2+1) (z_D) -- both admissible M palindromic. SCOPE-(a) PRUNE, NOT a characterisation: 'z - h/2 bar-invariant' defines an INFINITE family (one non-admissible member is exhibited), so a functional failing the test is excluded but one passing it is not thereby admissible. No anchor and no experimental input enter the parity test; the numeric section is calibration only. Nothing wired.

scope.established: both admissible roots satisfy z - bar(z) = h and give bar(Q)/Q = q^3; the published z = 1 and the excised z_C both fail, both by being bar-INVARIANT
scope.NOT_established: that bar-parity characterises admissibility — the criterion defines an infinite family and CHECK 4 exhibits a member that is not an admissible root
scope.use: a candidate Q_beta functional FAILING the parity is excluded; one passing it is not thereby admissible. Runs with no anchor and no experimental input, so it prunes before any number is computed.
